code: kl_gaussian_convolution <- function(p_ref, p_alt, mu, Sigma) {   mean_ref <- drop(mu %*% p_ref)   mean_alt <- drop(mu %*% p_alt)   cov_ref <- .compute_global_variance(p_ref, Sigma)   cov_alt <- .compute_global_variance(p_alt, Sigma)   precision_alt <- solve(cov_alt)   shift <- mean_alt - mean_ref   0.5 *     (sum(diag(precision_alt %*% cov_ref)) -       nrow(cov_ref) +       drop(t(shift) %*% precision_alt %*% shift) +       as.numeric(determinant(cov_alt, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus) -       as.numeric(determinant(cov_ref, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus)) }  p_reference <- c(0.4, 0.6) information <- expected_fisher_unconstrained(   p_reference,   mean_signature,   Sigma_iso ) steps <- c(1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4) data.frame(   step = steps,   kullback_leibler = vapply(     steps,     function(h) {       kl_gaussian_convolution(         p_reference,         p_reference + c(h, -h / 2),         mean_signature,         Sigma_iso       )     },     numeric(1)   ),   quadratic_form = vapply(     steps,     function(h) {       d <- c(h, -h / 2)       0.5 * drop(t(d) %*% information %*% d)     },     numeric(1)   ) ) #>    step kullback_leibler quadratic_form #> 1 1e-02     2.432446e-04   2.428254e-04 #> 2 1e-03     2.428691e-06   2.428254e-06 #> 3 1e-04     2.428298e-08   2.428254e-08

title: Simulating synthetic pseudo-bulk mixtures for benchmarking
text: vignette documents synthetic first- second-order moment generator simulate_hierarchical_grn_moments() outputs feed bulk mixture simulation. Mean profiles follow AutoGeneS-inspired construction (Aliee Theis 2021) single dial \rho (target_cosine) sets pairwise collinearity cell-type columns \boldsymbol{\mu}, fixed scale s (mean_scale) sets column norms. Prefer varying \rho across scenarios precision weights already control second-order dependence. cell type carries graph-constrained signed precision \boldsymbol{\Omega}_j, mapped \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j=\boldsymbol{\Omega}_j^{-1}. undirected Gaussian Markov simulation separates four layers (Equation 12): graph G_j, signed weights W(G_j), SPD precision \Omega_j, latent Gaussians (optional observation layer can add Poisson–log-normal zero-inflated counts). graph precision must conflated: binary adjacency almost never positive definite. DeCovarT draws G_j via generate_random_network_skeleton(), completes \Omega_j\succ 0 build_normalised_precision(), stacks inverted slices build_covariance_array_from_precision(). Section 4 develops topology, weight, SPD design detail.

title: Covariance-Aware Deconvolution of Bulk Transcriptomic Samples
text: DeCovarT R package bulk transcriptomic deconvolution accounts gene–gene covariance purified reference populations. Bulk observations modelled Gaussian convolutions cell-type means covariances, cellular proportions recovered open simplex via unconstrained (additive logistic) parametrisation. main entry point deconvolute_ratios(), runs one solvers parallel returns estimated proportions plus optional benchmark metrics.

title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: Evaluated log-sum-exp shift \(p_i\propto\exp(\tilde{\rho}_i-\max_k\tilde{\rho}_k)\) \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{J-1},0)\), algebraically identical ratio never forms \(\mathrm{e}^{\rho_i}\) directly. naive quotient overflows NaN \(\rho_i\gtrsim 710\), unconstrained ascent can reach MLE approaches simplex face; shifted form returns exact zero instead keeps \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) positive definite.

what: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
title: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
text: probability vector \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\) \(J\) classes (: cell types), Shannon entropy $$   H(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j \log p_j, $$ convention \(0\log 0 = 0\). Dividing maximum entropy \(\log J\) (uniform \(J\) classes) yields Pielou's evenness $$   H^{\star}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   \frac{H(\boldsymbol{p})}{\log J}   \[0,1], $$ \(H^{\star}=0\) Dirac mass one type \(H^{\star}=1\) uniform distribution \(J\) cell types. Zero masses dropped inside sum; normaliser still uses original class count \(J\). preferable changing logarithm base number positive masses \(J'\), renormalise support hide sparsity relative full panel cell types.

title: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
text: Estimates \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}=\arg\max_{\boldsymbol{p}} \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})\) Gaussian convolution model $$   \boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})   \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\bigr),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j, $$ subject simplex constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1\), \(\boldsymbol{p}\ge\mathbf{0}\). Optimisation performed unconstrained coordinates \(\boldsymbol{\rho}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\) via \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\) (Marquardt–Levenberg default; see methods vignette("generative-model-derivatives", package = "DeCovarT")).

title: Fit the DeCovarT Gaussian-convolution model — fit_decovart
text: Standardisation. CIBERSORT requires non-negative expression, missing values, non-log linear scale (Newman et al. 2015) . logarithm concave, Jensen's inequality shifts first second moments \(\log(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\neq(\log\boldsymbol{\mu})\boldsymbol{p}\). gene-wise affine map \(\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto D^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{m})\) \(D,\boldsymbol{m}\) \(\boldsymbol{Y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j^\star=D^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j D^{-1}\) leaves MLE \(\boldsymbol{p}\) unchanged (equivariance). Wald covariance. Let \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). expected Fisher information unconstrained mean–covariance map (multivariate normal; see e.g. Wikipedia entry Fisher information, multivariate normal) $$   (\boldsymbol{p})_{jk}   =   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\top}   \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   +   2 p_j p_k\,   \mathrm{tr}\bigl(     \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j     \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k   \bigr). $$ Cramer–Rao gives \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\rho}})\succeq I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1}\) ALR coordinates, \(I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}} =\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top} (\boldsymbol{p}) \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\) \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\partial\boldsymbol{\psi}/\partial\boldsymbol{\rho}^{\top}\) (jacobian_additive_logistic()). delta method maps bound back simplex: $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top}. $$

text: Builds \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\) blending shared unit direction \(\boldsymbol{u}\) cell-type-private orthogonal marker directions \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\): $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}   =   \sqrt{\rho}\,\boldsymbol{u}   +\sqrt{1-\rho}\,\boldsymbol{v}_{j},   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}   =   s\,   \frac{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}}{     \|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}\|_2   }. $$ private vectors \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) indicator directions partition \(G\) genes (type \(j\) ) \(\ell_2\)-normalised, \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}=0\) \(j\neq k\). shared unit \(\boldsymbol{u}\), $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot k}   =   \rho   +   \sqrt{\rho(1-\rho)}\,   \bigl(     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}     +     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}   \bigr)   \qquad (j\neq k). $$ column normalisation pairwise cosines \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) therefore track \(\rho\) closely cross terms \(\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) small relative leading \(\rho\) (many genes per block). global scale \(s\) sets column norms (hence Euclidean separation) without changing angles: fixed \(\rho\), \(\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2 \propto s\). Prefer dialling \(\rho\) second-order precision weights already control interaction strength; keep \(s\) fixed across scenarios compare mean collinearity alone (Aliee Theis 2021) .

Hold fixed studying cosine / collinearity alone. target_cosine Numeric \([0,1]\), collinearity dial \(\rho\). gene_names Optional character vector length \(G\). celltype_names Optional character vector length \(J\).

title: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
text: Private marker blocks. Genes partitioned \(J\) nearly equal contiguous blocks. Type \(j\)'s private direction \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) indicator block, \(\ell_2\)-normalised. Distinct blocks orthogonal, type-specific signal leak across columns shared component added. Shared–private blend. unit shared direction \(\boldsymbol{u}=G^{-1/2}\mathbf{1}\), column \(\sqrt{\rho}\,\boldsymbol{u}+\sqrt{1-\rho}\,\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\), re-normalised, scaled \(s\). Thus \(\rho\) dials collinearity \(s\) dials Euclidean separation without changing angles.

title: Gradient \(\nabla_{\boldsymbol{p}}\ell\) of the unconstrained log-likelihood — gradient_loglik_unconstrained
text: Analytic gradient loglik_multivariate() respect \(\boldsymbol{p}\). Writing \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\) \(\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}\), \(j\)-th coordinate $$   \frac{\partial\ell}{\partial p_j}   =   -p_j\,\mathrm{Tr}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\bigr)   +\boldsymbol{r}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}   +p_j\,\boldsymbol{r}^{\mathsf{T}}   \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{r}. $$ determinant score \(-p_j\mathrm{Tr}(\boldsymbol{\Theta} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) \(\partial\boldsymbol{\Sigma}/\partial p_j=2p_j\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\) enters \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\); two residual terms unaffected factor.

title: Unconstrained DeCovarT log-likelihood — loglik_multivariate
text: additive constant independent \(\boldsymbol{p}\), $$   \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})   -\tfrac{1}{2}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})^{\mathsf{T}}   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}). $$ terms carry factor \(1/2\) Gaussian log-density. earlier release used \(-\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\), doubled determinant contribution left objective inconsistent expected_fisher_unconstrained(). factor restored, \(\mathbb{E}[-\mathbf{H}]=(\boldsymbol{p})\) exactly. Computationally Cholesky--backsolve evaluation mvtnorm::dmvnorm(..., log = TRUE) (Genz Bretz), omitting additive \(-\tfrac{G}{2}\log(2\pi)\) depend \(\boldsymbol{p}\). cached factor .sigma_p_factorisation() supplies upper-triangular \(\boldsymbol{R}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{R}\); Mahalanobis term \(\lVert\boldsymbol{R}^{-\mathsf{T}} (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\rVert^{2}\), obtained base::backsolve() without forming explicit inverse. inverse still cached analytic score Hessian need \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}(\boldsymbol{p}) =\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). QR factorisation \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) expensive route SPD quantities; Cholesky natural factorisation. Argument mean_signature_matrix stores plug-mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\). Latent sample-specific profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}\) observed; frequentist likelihood treats \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) fixed proxy. Estimating latents jointly \(\boldsymbol{p}\) requires Bayesian / MAP step (see .map_gaussian_convolution()).

Boundary null. null \(p_j=0\) lets parameter move one direction , local parameter space half-line rather vector space Wilks' theorem fails. limit chi-bar-square mixture chi_bar_square_pvalue(): single active constraint, \(D\rightsquigarrow\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{1}\) Chernoff (1954) , generalised several active constraints Self Liang (1987) . title: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
text: bootstrap sample \(=1,\ldots,N\), draws latent purified profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\sim   \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) independently cell type \(j=1,\ldots,J\), forms bulk linear convolution $$   \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }   =\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\boldsymbol{p}   =\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}, $$ matching article's conditional model \(\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})\sim \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}))\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})= \sum_j p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\). mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) shared across samples; latent draws \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\) vary \(\). Stacking draws three-way array \(\mathcal{X}=(x_{gji})\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J\times N}\), bulk matrix mode-2 tensor–vector contraction $$   \boldsymbol{Y}   =\mathcal{X}\times_{2}\boldsymbol{p},   \qquad   y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}x_{gji}\,p_{j}   \quad(g=1,\ldots,G;\; =1,\ldots,N), $$ sample recovers \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\,\boldsymbol{p}\) \(\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\).

what: Cramer–Rao / ALR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_alr_delta
title: Cramer–Rao / ALR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_alr_delta
text: Maps expected Fisher information unconstrained proportions additive log-ratio (ALR) chart back simplex via delta method. Let \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\partial\boldsymbol{\psi}/\partial\boldsymbol{\rho}^{\top}\) (jacobian_additive_logistic()). Fisher information transforms covariant quadratic form $$   I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top}   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}. $$ regular large-sample regime MLE ALR coordinates asymptotically normal, \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\rho}} \overset{}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\rho}_{0}, I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1})\) (Cramer–Rao / asymptotic normality MLEs; law large numbers score). first-order delta method yields simplex covariance used vcov.decovart_fit() Wald standard errors confint.decovart_fit(): $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   \approx   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{\rho}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top}. $$ Diagonal square roots matrix asymptotic standard errors; Wald intervals level \(1-\alpha\) \(\hat{p}_j \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\,\mathrm{SE}_j\) \(z_{q}=\Phi^{-1}(q)\). construction undefined simplex boundary (ALR chart blows ); function returns NA warning. See also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_method https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information#Multivariate_normal_distribution.
